root_cause.text: The mt76 DMA cleanup logic incorrectly assumed only NAPI-associated RX queues needed cleanup, so WED RRO RX queues’ page_pool allocations and buffers were skipped during device teardown, causing a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “All MT76 rx queues have an associated page_pool even if the queue is not associated to a NAPI (e.g. WED RRO queues with WED enabled)” and the patch removes the `continue` in `mt76_dma_cleanup()` that skipped WED RRO queues, while adding page return logic in `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup()` for WED RRO queues when WED is not active.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The mt76 DMA cleanup logic incorrectly assumed only NAPI-associated RX queues needed cleanup, so WED RRO RX queues’ page_pool allocations and buffers were skipped during device teardown, causing a memory leak.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message states “All MT76 rx queues have an associated page_pool even if the queue is not associated to a NAPI (e.g. WED RRO queues with WED enabled)” and the patch removes the `continue` in `mt76_dma_cleanup()` that skipped WED RRO queues, while adding page return logic in `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup()` for WED RRO queues when WED is not active.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip cleanup and page-pool freeing for active WED RRO-managed RX queues to avoid incorrectly releasing hardware-managed buffers.
intent_record.what: In `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup`, the single condition `if (!mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q)) mt76_put_page_pool_buf(buf, false);` was replaced with two checks: first, if `mtk_wed_device_active(&dev->mmio.wed)` is true and `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q)` is true, the loop skips further handling with `continue`; second, page-pool buffers are freed only when the queue is neither `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro_rxdmad_c(q)` nor `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro_ind(q)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, cleanup now avoids processing active WED RRO queues in this path and narrows buffer release so that buffers belonging to specific WED RRO-related queue types are not returned to the page pool here. This prevents incorrect cleanup/freeing of buffers that are managed differently when WED is active.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always clean up WED RRO RX queues during mt76 DMA teardown so their NAPI state and DMA resources are not left behind.
intent_record.what: The change removes a conditional early-continue inside the RX queue cleanup loop in mt76_dma_cleanup(), specifically deleting the check for an active WED device combined with mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q), so netif_napi_del(&dev->napi[i]) and mt76_dma_rx_cleanup(dev, q) now run for all RX queues.
intent_record.how: At runtime, RX queues marked as WED RRO are no longer skipped during DMA cleanup when WED is active, ensuring their NAPI instances are deleted and their RX DMA resources are cleaned up as part of device teardown. This prevents those queues from being left initialized or leaking resources during cleanup.

Always clean up WED RRO RX queues during mt76 DMA teardown so their NAPI state and DMA resources are not left behind.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly modifies RX queue cleanup/page-pool freeing behavior for WED RRO-managed queues, which is the same teardown logic involved in the root cause. It addresses how those queues are handled during cleanup, making it directly related to the vulnerability.
The change directly fixes the root cause by ensuring WED RRO RX queues are also cleaned up during mt76 DMA teardown, preventing skipped page_pool/buffer cleanup and the resulting memory leak.

This conditional begins the logic that incorrectly assumes active WED RRO RX queues should be excluded from DMA teardown, directly leading to skipped cleanup.
This condition identifies WED RRO RX queues as the special case to exclude; combined with the following continue, it is the specific gate that leaves those queues uncleared.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement skips teardown for queues matching the preceding WED-active/WED-RRO condition, causing WED RRO RX queues to bypass cleanup and leak their page_pool allocations and buffers.
This conditional starts the faulty exclusion logic that treats active WED RRO RX queues as queues that should not be cleaned up during DMA teardown.
This condition component selects WED RRO RX queues as the special case for exclusion, which when combined with the continue causes the cleanup omission behind the memory leak.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body for `mt76_dma_cleanup()` is sufficient to evaluate the specific cleanup behavior present in this commit. It cleans TX queues with `for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(dev->q_tx); i++) mt76_dma_tx_cleanup(dev, i, true);` and RX queues only with `for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(dev->q_rx); i++) { netif_napi_del(&dev->napi[i]); mt76_dma_rx_cleanup(dev, &dev->q_rx[i]); }`. The root cause described requires the existence of additional WED RRO RX queues whose page_pool allocations/buffers are outside the normal NAPI-associated `dev->q_rx[]` cleanup path. In this 2017 commit, there is no WED/RRO logic, no page_pool handling, and no extra RX queue list beyond `dev->q_rx[]`. Therefore the vulnerable construct tied to skipping WED RRO RX queues is not present in this function version. At the same time, the later fix is also not present here, because there is no broader cleanup mechanism for non-`q_rx[]` RX queues—only the basic `q_rx[]` loop exists.
